id: HWA1 (dev PC draft 2026-11-19, registered by the robot PC): hold-layer ablation vs ours on the real G1, steps disabled, same environment
question: Without steps, does the hold-first layer let the robot hold lateral pushes that the same controller without it (hold-first never entered) cannot? Development (robot PC 11-19, not registered): ours 17/17 lateral 28-83 N held; ablation 25-36 N held, 46.8 N stopped by the loop guard (guard asymmetry, now fixed by DEPLOY_GUARD_PUSH_EX).

arms.ablation: identical command and env plus --theta_d 100000 (the hold-first entry threshold is never reached; everything else, incl. the estimator, the MPC and the ID, is identical)

setup: both arms: DEPLOY_GUARD_PUSH_EX=25,1.0 (loop guard exempt on the controller-independent push signal for both arms), DEPLOY_GUARD_KNEE=0.6, tilt guard 15 deg, gantry as HWD1. Env + commit written into HWA1_config.txt and hashed with this file.
pushes: shoulder-height lateral hand pushes through the load cell, horizontal, normal release, plateau aimed 30-80 N in an ascending series per block (30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 N aimed), held 0.3-0.5 s; one side per block; blocks alternate ours / ablation (ours first in session 1, ablation first in session 2); >= 5 s quiet between pushes. A block ends after its series or after a failure.
amount: FIXED number of blocks: 6 blocks per arm per session (3 per side), two sessions (12 blocks per arm). Each block = one ascending series (aimed 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 N), ended by the series or by a failure; a block is never extended or repeated because of its outcome. Changed from the draft ('>= 24 counted pushes per arm in 40-80 N, else inconclusive'): with blocks ending at a failure the arm that fails earlier contributes fewer pushes in range, so a push-count rule would be confounded with the outcome.
counting: as HWD1 / HWL1: load-cell plateau >= 20 N, lateral by the kinematic direction rule (HWL1 amendment 3), excluded without controller outputs: pre-push stick contact > 3 N, a foot lift or guard stop before the onset, a second contact within 3 s.
outcome: held = HWL1 amendment-7 rule as used in HWD1 (no foot lift, tilt rise < 12 deg (HWD1 amendment 2), knee > 0.6 rad, no guard stop, within 3 s after the load cell falls below 8 N). A guard stop of any kind counts as not held for both arms (the loop-guard asymmetry is removed by the push exemption).

predictions.A1 (primary): block score = highest load-cell plateau among the block's counted HELD pushes (0 if none); ours > ablation, one-sided Mann-Whitney U over the blocks, alpha 0.05
predictions.A2 (secondary): counted pushes with plateau 40-80 N: held proportion ours > ablation, one-sided Fisher exact (reported; the push numbers are outcome-dependent, see amount)
predictions.reported: per block first failed plateau and failure modes; held / failed against impulse per arm (figure); peak tilt / CoM excursion of held pushes; compute time per tick; hold-first ticks per block (arm check: 0 for every ablation block, else the block is excluded)

limitations_stated_in_advance: Pushes are unpaired (hand pushes differ between arms); the force range and alternating blocks limit the imbalance, the impulse plot shows it. The ablation keeps the MPC's own disturbance compensation; it is the hold layer that is tested, not the estimator (E1/E2 test the estimator).
analysis: to be written on the dev PC before registration (hwa1_analyze.py, counting and held rule from hwl1_analyze.py, as hwd1_analyze.py); dry run by the robot PC on the 11-19 development recordings (151057 ablation, 135553 ours), then hashed with this file and HWA1_config.txt.
manuscript_use: If run: one sentence and a panel next to H1 in the hardware section (the hold layer, not only the estimate, is what holds on hardware), whatever the outcome.
H0_gate: before the first counted block: one 60 s quiet recording (label hwa1_quiet_s1) with DEPLOY_GUARD_PUSH_EX on and no push: the guard log must show quiet ticks (loop guard active) and no trip; engineering check, not a result.
registered: 2026-11-19 ~15:30 local, robot PC, before any HWA1 recording. Analysis: experiments/robust_holdability/hwa1_analyze.py, written by the robot PC (the dev PC had offered to write it; disclosed), dry run on the two development recordings of 11-19 (135553 ours, 151057 ablation; not part of HWA1): ours 16 counted, score 63.9 N, first failure 62.3 N; ablation 3 counted, score 0 (29.0 / 31.6 N foot lift, 39.5 N tilt / DAMP); arm check 1173 / 0 hold ticks. Design changes against the draft: amount (fixed blocks) and A1 (block-level Mann-Whitney, the draft's Fisher test kept as A2). Config: HWA1_config.txt (hashed).
amendment 1: 2026-11-19 ~16:05 local, robot PC, after session 1 and BEFORE any HWA1 outcome analysis (no held / failed rule and no A1 / A2 statistic computed; seen: per-block QC = deploy config, hold-first tick counts, load-cell push peaks, and that every block ended on a guard). (a) Excluded recordings (operator set-up, decided by the operator's account and the deploy config, not by outcomes): g1lc_20261119_153424_hwa1_ours_s1_b1_L (ran with --theta_d 100000 and without DEPLOY_GUARD_PUSH_EX - wrong config; re-run as 154024); g1lc_20261119_154458_hwa1_abl_s1_b2_R (operator set-up error, no push; the block is 154543 in the same deploy run); g1lc_20261119_154858_hwa1_ours_s1_b4_R (operator set-up error by the operator's account - it ended on the knee guard after one 38 N push, disclosed; the block is 154939). (b) Series overshoot: ours blocks continued past the registered 80 N step (8-15 pushes, peaks to 160 N). The block score (A1) is capped at 80 N (min(highest held plateau, 80)); A2 already uses 40-80 N. (c) Session 2: exactly one push per aimed level 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 N, block ends after the 80 N push or a failure.
amendment 2: 2026-11-19 ~16:35 local, robot PC, after session 2 and BEFORE any HWA1 outcome analysis (QC only: config, hold ticks, push peaks, block-ending guards). Decision of the experimenter (operator): every repeated block was a restart because of the experimenter's inexperience (set-up / handling), and the repeat is the block. Disclosed facts: all repeats were of OURS blocks and each first attempt had ended on a guard after 1-4 pushes with the registered config (THR 25, PUSH_EX on): s1 b4_R 154858 (knee, after 38 N), s2 b2_R 161051 (knee, after 25/36/44 N), s2 b3_L 161348 (knee, after 32/44 N), s2 b6_R 162140 (tilt, after 30/31/41/57 N); no ablation block was repeated. Primary analysis (A1, A2): repeats replace the first attempts (exclusions listed in hwa1_analyze.EXCLUDE). Reported alongside, same tests: FIRST-ATTEMPT analysis (each block = its first config-valid deploy run; hwa1_analyze.py --first). Further rules: a block = one deploy run; recordings of the same label within one deploy run are merged (abl s2 b1_L 160622 + 160736; empty logger starts 154458, 160609 have no push); 153424 stays excluded in both analyses (wrong config). Block score cap 80 N (amendment 1) applies (session 2 again exceeded the series, peaks to 103 N). Operator impression (unblinded, the operator knew the arm): 'as the pusher, ours clearly holds and resists better'.
amendment 3: 2026-11-19 ~16:50 local, robot PC, experimenter's decision: the first-attempt analysis of amendment 2 is dropped (not reported). It was stopped while running and its output deleted unread - no first-attempt result was seen by anyone. The disclosed facts about the repeated blocks (amendment 2) stay. Primary analysis unchanged.
amendment 4 (clarification): 2026-11-19 ~17:30 local, robot PC, clarification of amendment 2 by the experimenter: the four restarted ours blocks (s1 b4_R, s2 b2_R, s2 b3_L, s2 b6_R) were restarted because the robot caught on the set-up (harness / structure) and went down - a set-up failure, not a response to the push. The guard that ended each first attempt (knee / tilt) is the logged consequence of that fall. The original recordings are kept. Nothing else changes.
